title: Its not what it was
content:
Now that the old deshimula post era has died down, I will try to write this down as a full and overall review of what and how this company functions as a whole. My intention being that I am writing this for people who will join this company, and not as a feedback to the company. Beause I feel nobody takes feedback here at all. I wrote a lot of this on my last review and nobody cared and nobody even reached out to me to ask why I wrote such harsh words there, so I am posting here instead.
First off, this is a pretty good place if you are young in your career and look forward to work in a global role. Opti has no local clients (and thus no local impact on work). Infact, 100% of the revenue comes from SaaS Software and relevant services sales from mostly USA/EU clients. This has lots of advantages - such as great learning opportunities, good exposure, and is very good on your resume. Before joining Opti nobody would knock me on LinkedIn and offer jobs. Now they do. I guess that explains it all.
But there are lots of disadvantages there too. Opti is not a heaven for everyone. There are bad bosses, bad managers, and bad teams as much as there are good ones. I don't mind those because thats just bad luck. The real problem is that there are lots of layoffs, and silent downsizing almost every month. The overall vibe from the company is very down, or atleast thats what I see in Dhaka and even from my colleagues abroad. They will tell you that sales is good on the townhall, and go back and fire 15 people that they just hired last quarter. They will tell you how things are well, and then cut down on basic costs the next day and say its a cost decision.
Look, I have worked in lots of frugal companies.
Frugality isn't to be confused with mis-management and lack of planning.
Just last week, a guy was fired within 5 months of hiring. They say the role is no longer open and they need someone senior. It broke my heart. This guy was just hired right out of university. You took many interviews. You even gave him good feedback on his 1:1s about his work performance. And then you say you need someone senior? Is someones life a joke to you? Who took the multiple interviews, found him fit for the role, and finally hired him? Why wasn't that person fired instead? Which HR person didn't filter for a more senior role instead? Why did the department head sign off on the budget knowing that you can only attract juniors with that kind of budget? Absolutely zero empathy!
You might feel its a one off issue and there is something I don't know about this case. But bro, this is like the 30th time this is happening in this company. The lack of planning and foresight is crazy. If you can't retain why are you hiring? How will new people joining the company feel that they could be laid off next day? Its not even like its a major cost decision because literal straight out of uni kids are being fired sometimes. How much do they even earn? Its crazy how people are treated like objects here. And its excerbated by the fact that HR here is run by people from Vietnam who have no local context and zero understanding of local scenarios of how hiring and firing should be done.
And oh, lets not even talk about how HR does not help these laid off folks in any way whatsoever. They are asked themselves to apply to other roles in the company and nobody helps them out even with a referral or priority. Couldn't you just go ahead and make it a priority to retain them in another team instead? How difficult would it be for HR to tell HR that they have other roles open where this person can function just as well! Why wasn't there any attempt to secure them a role with the 10 other open ones? I have been here for 3 years and haven't seen anybody planning my career growth or had any discussion with any BP around my JD or how I can grow. Its a job handed off to managers nowadays and its impossible to do these discussions with any manager in any real company, but HR thinks its not their job. Actually HR thinks nothing is their job. They are just busy instagramming their 4th vacation this year while finance is blamed for all problems in this company. Ridiculous, to say the least.
So yes, if you are joining this company check whether this role just had a layoff last week. Check how many people here didn't even have a proper manager for months after months because people were laid off abroad without any planning. Check why their offer to you is almost 50% of their actual budget and what they are paying someone else in the same role (something I got to know after joining). The problem is that there is no BP planning how the business will continue to function, and you will be put on the hot seat and judged for it barely months after joining. Make sure you are ready for that kind of judgement instead of support.
But lets say we disregard this. What happened after there were all of these DM posts saying bad things about the company? Was anything addressed at all?
Yes the HR Head came down and told us that she she wants girls to wear different clothes instead of telling the creeps to back off. Life wtf, are you insinuating that people coming in naked to the office in the name of "localization" and "understanding cultural context"? It is an American company. If my counterpart in USA can wear a skirt, why not me here? Isn't that the values that I was told about when I joined? Where did those values go? Under the shirts and tops that you no longer want? There was zero support from the leadership around this and instead the vietnamese management got involved and just asked rude questions to try and pat down everyone. I hate how I was told "You have to prioritize company decisions" like I am a 12 year old kid who is being taught how to behave. Look, I live in Dhaka. I have been fighting these radicals all my life. I will fight you too if it comes to that. I have no problems with fighting all of you when it comes to letting my girls wear whatever they want. Its your duty to make them comfortable, not the radical ones. This was ridiculous as a manager for me to face questions from my team and having to say that I have no support. And hell, one specefic girl was attacked for her choice of clothes and she wasn't given any vocal support from anybody in leadership! SHE NO LONGER COMES TO OFFICE - BECAUSE OF YOU GUYS! Some senior engineers were attacked by what looked like bullies in their team and one guy resigned himself but had no support from HR at all. I know those guys and I can vouch that the bullies had no right to demean them and there was no bold learship move that we don't believe in this bullying and we support them throughout!
Is this how HR should function in a global org? Actually now most of the girls who were attacked just dont come to office anymore. Because they don't feel safe. My team mates have told me multiple times that they feel odd about going to office knowing there are people judging them there. What did HR do about that? Absolutely nothing! I heard of one case where there was a direct SH complaint but nothing was done by HR at all. Now the girl does WFH and the guy is in the office with his teeth wide open. If you don't believe me then just go to the old TA Table on a random day and see how its empty and devoid and looks like a ghost town. That was the liveliest bunch of people in Dhaka and if they are not coming to the office anymore then you guys have done something seriously wrong as a company. They are coasting, and all of them will leave when they can. Its visible. And this is purely a management failure. When the old founders from their newsroom days came I thought things will change and people will see improvement. But honestly, I see no change and no initiative these days.
And then there is the raise issue. Opti will agree to a relatively high joining salary but not offer any decent increments after that. But they will spend millions on random events across the world instead with no real value or ROI. There is no real adjustment for inflation here at all. Infact I am getting paid less this year than last year due to changes in tax structure too. So keep this in mind.
Negotiate real hard on the joining salary because you will be stuck with less than this in a year or two.
They will say they sold hundreds of millions extra and pipe is great on the townhall, but when it comes to raises they will tell you business is bad and you should understand etc etc. They regularly expect Dhaka people to do late night office but they don't even bother to reimburse costs or even keep the office open or even pay over time. Infact there is no fixed working hours, which turns into a serious issue after a while. People abroad will regularly schedule 1 AM calls even though my office ends at 10: and then I am expected to either attend the call or fall back on my own. How can this be a culture as a company? Nobody in vietnam takes late night calls. Nobody in USA does either. Why just us?
And oh, what about training? Why is there no training at all here? Who should be in charge of that? You say you want seniors, but you hire only juniors, and then its my headache to teach them everything? You are just slowing down the rest of the company here with these decisions.
Look my final verdict is this: if you are a young proffessional, opti dhaka is a good place to join for your first job and gain some experience and move out as soon as you can.
Because this company can't retain folks who are worth two cents.
Anybody worth two cents will go away in a few years because they dont get raises, trainings, and for career growth they just have to wait for the people infront to be laid off first. And thats just reality.
Someone at opti told me a long time ago that you should judge a company by its average age. The lower the average age of employees, the worse culure it will have. I found that silly. Why would a young population mean something is wrong? Young folks are the best! But now I understand what he meant. Companies that can't retain people for long can't really do great things - because the people with experience are leaving for better land across the ocean. The young are just too young just don't know when to jump ship yet.
All the best and I am writing to you all knowing that some of you will disagree but most will agree. And I understand. Just give it some time. I will see you at the Airport soon.

title: A Company Built by Its People Deserves Better.
content:
I have recently come across several posts on DeshiMula. Initially I was not following them very closely. It is not that I am indifferent. I just did not have the time or energy to go through everything being said. However I do appreciate the purpose of this platform. Giving professionals a voice and allowing them to reflect on their work experiences is a valuable initiative and one that deserves recognition.
Regarding Opt!m!zly I want to start by saying that no company is perfect. Every workplace has its strengths and weaknesses. I have read a number of the recent reviews and some of them make fair points. Constructive feedback is important and when offered with good intent it can help leadership identify areas for growth. Whether or not those insights lead to actual changes is up to the people in charge.
What pushed me to write this post is not disagreement with criticism. It is the way some of the criticism has turned personal. It is disappointing to see posts targeting individuals with hostility. Many of the people being criticised have spent years building the very environment we now benefit from. I have had the chance to interact with some of them both professionally and informally. Despite their seniority they have always treated me with respect and made time to support when needed. That level of professionalism deserves to be acknowledged.
Of course nobody is perfect. Not the leadership. Not the employees. Not me either. We all have flaws and yes we all sometimes complain or gossip. But there is a difference between sharing thoughts with a colleague and publishing personal attacks on a public platform. If someone genuinely caused harm by blocking a promotion or creating a toxic experience I hope that it was addressed with a manager or through HR before being made public. If not then it raises the question of whether the goal was improvement or just public venting.
Life is always about trade-offs. To offer an analogy consider the residential area of Bashundhara R A. It has many challenges. Some say there are not enough mosques. Others mention the distance to grocery stores or the nearby university students' lifestyle that might not appeal to everyone. Still many people choose to live there. They might have a child studying in a nearby school or university. Or maybe it is closer to work. Or maybe it provides a better security then other areas. And those who cannot adjust simply move somewhere else. No one forces anyone to stay.
The same applies to workplaces. If the culture or environment does not suit someone they have every right to leave. But leaving with grace is very different from trying to tear down what remains. Especially when others still work there and appreciate what has been built.
Opt!m!zly is a global company. We work with colleagues from a wide range of cultures religions and personal backgrounds. Naturally there will be differences in lifestyle and beliefs. But our purpose here is not to push personal ideologies. It is to perform learn grow and contribute within a global professional setting.
I also want to point out something important. The job market is connected in more ways than we often realize. When someone speaks negatively about their workplace online it creates an impression that may follow them. If I were hiring and I saw a organization name associated with public hostility towards from their employees, I would hesitate and think carefully before bringing that person into my team regardless how talented that person is. Talent is valuable but team culture matters too.
I am not defending every decision made by leadership. This message is not about taking sides. It is simply a call for professionalism and perspective. Respect your workplace. And if it does not feel right anymore seek opportunities that align better with your long term goals. Do it with maturity.
To the leadership team at Opt!m!zly both past and present I want to say that there are many of us who see your effort and dedication. We may not always say it out loud but your contributions are noticed and appreciated.
To everyone reading this I hope this comes across in the spirit it is intended. If I have unintentionally offended anyone that was not my intention. I am simply offering a viewpoint from one professional to another. Wishing you all continued growth and success in your careers and lives.

title: A Titanic in the making
content:
Once a company known for its culture and ability to attract the best talent in the market, now turned into a ticking time bomb about to go off. Every day someone somewhere around the globe is leaving or is getting fired, management has no idea what to do, has been this way ever since.  A big big reason high level directors, managers and team leads worth their salt are leaving before going down with the ship.
This is a big no-no for anyone in their mid/high level career because this company can neither provide the growth nor the stability you need, and no it's not something you can overturn with your performance or vigor.
There is subtle racism when working with foreign teams, perks of being a low-cost labor from 3rd third-world country, you would never get an invitation to attend the high-level decision making meetings, just a worker assigned to follow orders once they are revealed.
All that being said, it is the perfect company for Gen Z peeps in their early career, hardly any micromanagement, insane level of flexibility, salary is really good compared to the country median. Basically anyone who wants to add a few months of job experience in their cv while preparing for abroad, you cannot ask for anything better but beware do fall under the comfort zone trap, before you know it you will either lose chance at a good career or get kicked out randomly and become a floater.

title: পাড়ার মাস্তান আর চুন্নীদের আড্ডা
content:
একজন মাস্তানকে কয়েকদিন আগে কোম্পানী ফায়ার করার পর তার অবস্থানে তারই ঘনিষ্ট ফ্রেন্ডকে বসানো হয়। সব টাকা পয়সা সামলানো তার রেসপন্সিবিলিটি হওয়ায় সেই মাস্তান আর তার পা চাটার দল মনে করে যে অফিসিয়াল ট্যুরে গিয়ে ফ্যামিলিসুদ্ধ সব এমপ্লয়িদের মদ গেলানো তাদের একান্ত ফরজ। তাদের আড্ডায় TA নামক শাকচুন্নীরাও সামিল হয় যাদেরক স্যালারী দেয়ার পরও ফকিন্নির মত আসল রেফারারের নাম সরায়ে নিজের নাম বসায়ে রেফারাল বোনাস হাতায়ে নেয়। এই চুরির পর, চাকরী যাওয়ার পরেও এরা অফিসে এসে আরামে ঘুরে যায়। রাতে এদের মদ্যপানের আসর জমে অফিসে।
মাস্তান গ্রুপটার নিজেদের মধ্যে হেডম আর নেপোটিজমের শেষ নাই। এমনিতে অন্যদের কখনো বিন্দু পরিমাণ পাত্তা না দিলেও এখন নতুন লোকেশন চ্যাম্পিয়ন (কালচারাল হেড) ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং ডিরেক্টর হওয়াতে সেই ডিরেক্টরকে দিন রাত চাটাচাটিতে ব্যস্ত থাকে মাস্তানগুলা। ডিরেক্টরও ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং চিন্তা বাদ দিয়ে তাদের আড্ডায় সামিল হয়। ডিরেক্টরের না আছে কোন ভিশন, না আছে কোন প্রোডাক্ট নলেজ, মাঝে মাঝে মনে হয় স্পাইনটাও ক্ষয়ে যাচ্ছে।

title: Show off, favoritism, bootlicking - you name it
content: Once a stellar engineering company with a vibrant culture and strong values, it has deteriorated into chaos. The glossy social media facade hides a grim reality. Promotions and international transfers increasingly depend on oiling the upper management. The recently sacked finance director, known for excessive drinking, filled director roles with cronies, fostering a toxic culture of after-hours office drinking. The engineering director, lacking substantial experience, rose through self-promotion rather than merit. The company’s decline is disheartening.

title: Great people. Great place to work. Terrible last month.
content:
I don't want to say much because I have already left this company (thankfully) and have a much better role elsewhere. I miss Optimizely and all of the people there. Honestly, I do. I loved the work. I loved the engineers, the pms, the sales teams, the solutions guys, the commercial people, and even the support team. I see all of these complaints on DeshiMula and I can't vibe with them because back in our times, they were not there. But I also hated it the last few months. The way HR spoke to me once I told them I am planning to leave still has my ears ringing. The way they forced me to resign even though I had already communicated in advance that I am waiting for an update on something and would resign later. The way a guy on their team was absurdly rude to me. The way I could not even ask a question about the financial issues. The way they asked me to sign paperwork then and there immediately almost as if I am a criminal for deciding to accept a better offer. The way they weren't giving me a release letter and were chilling in some other country when it was important to me. I will never forget that.
It was odd how HR suddenly turned on me the moment I told them I found a better role! There was no proper exit debrief (shouldn't that be standard?) or else I wouldn't be writing it here. But I was hurt. And I will carry that feeling forever that this company treats you like shit once you leave. Just speak to some other people who have left and you will understand. Some of the guys who were in newscred had it different. It wasn't the same experience for us. Man, it wasn't even my manager. It was a bunch of sore losers who didn't even know me properly. I just wish I was in a financial position to throw the money in your face and walk away instead of having to go through that.

title: Rant to my own people!
content:
Been seeing lots of reviews about Optimizely lately - some useful, others just keyboard therapy. Here’s mine: honest, balanced, and to the point. If you’re here for real insight, not drama, read on:
Let’s start with the Cons (because y’all clearly love to start your day with negativity)
No more unlimited PTO
– A major perk gone; hurts flexibility.
Job security is shaky
– Layoffs and re-orgs create uncertainty.
Too comfy = career stagnation
– Long-term flexibility can make you unfit for local market (bidesh chara ar goti thakbena)
Low salary growth
: 6–8% annual raise (my case for the last 3 years) barely beats inflation.
Cost-cutting vibe
– Budget trims affecting morale.
Hiring team needs serious upskilling
– A very recent observed gap in hiring quality and industry understanding.
But here are the Pros (and they’re not imaginary, either):
Super Competitive salary
– Among the best in town (if not the best)
Office transport
– Free pickup and drop in Dhaka.
Flexible work
– Work from home, work in your PJs, work from Cox’s Bazar or Paharer Chura if you want (and if the WiFi holds). It’s a real blessing.
Global exposure
– This is one of the best parts; interacting with folks from different geographies, understanding how global companies operate, building that exposure. Seriously valuable for your long-term growth.
Provident Fund
– Announced with company contribution.
LTI program
– Recently launched, generous amount.
Free meals & snacks
– Decent daily office perks.
Top-tier colleagues
– Talented team with strong skills.
Annual retreats
- Fun, well-organized team events.
And now, the fun and best part: roasting the drama queens (or kings? What should I tell you?)
OMG no unlimited PTO = toxic company” -
Yes, it’s a bummer. But if that’s your whole personality now, maybe take one of your
limited
PTO days and go outside.
There’s no PF -
Brother, it was literally announced. Stop sleeping through meetings or skimming Slack like it’s a TikTok comment section.
Crying about the coffee machine
- Really bro? You’re getting paid decently. If it's not working sometime and thus it ruins your week, you might need to re-evaluate your priorities. Go buy yourself a caramel macchiato and move on
.
"Company sucks, management sucks, everything sucks”
- Then why are you still here, bro? If you hate it so much, go find a better place. Oh wait - you won’t. Because deep down, you know you won't find any better opportunity. I'm also searching over a year for a "better opportunity" but got nothing but your dramas around me. So you whine… keep on whining.... Why did you stop? Whine again? Pleaseee? It's way easier.
And let’s not forget the support we got during serious stuff - like when internet was cut during the student protests. Folks from other countries covered for us. My manager had my back, and for that, I’ll always be grateful. You don’t get that kind of empathy everywhere.
Finally, to Seniors, EAB, HR:
Please start by having real conversations with global leadership
.
Copy-pasting U.S. strategy to Bangladesh doesn’t work
. Here, job security is sacred. You fire someone in the U.S. - they get another job next week. Here? Not so simple. Explain the market, the culture, and the consequences. Otherwise, you all suck and are good for nothing!
HR team
, can we please talk?
When you sit together in a corner like a secret illuminaty society, it makes people (at least me) paranoid. Be more approachable. Mingle with the team like everyone else in the office. Be more human. Laura (CPO) set a great example - Please follow that energy.
Wrapping up:
No company is perfect. Optimizely isn’t either. But it’s not trash just because it’s not giving out coffee like Santa Claus or took away unlimited PTO.
If you’re writing a review, be
balanced
. Tell people what’s working and what’s not. Don’t take the good stuff for granted while building a whole rant around what you didn’t get.
Be real, or just keep scrolling.

title: চক চক করলেই সোনা হয়না
content: যাই করেন জীবনে, শুধু এক্সপেরিমেন্টেশন টিমে জয়েন কইরেন না। পুরা টিম ভর্তি সবাই শুধু একজন আরেকজনকে চাকু মারার তালে থাকে। সিনিয়র লিডারশিপ বলতে কিছু নাই ঢাকায়। যিনি আছে উনি না থাকার থেকেও ভালো। টিমের জন্য কিছুই করেনা। কোন ধরনের লিডারশিপ প্রেজেন্স নাই যে কারোর থেকে কিছু শিখবেন এই টিমে। সারাদিন সারারাত খাটাবে আর বলবে যে আগে প্রোজেক্ট ডেলিভার করো বাকিটা পরে দেখতেসি। বছর শেষ হইলে আসলে কিছুই দেখেনা। যাই ডেলিভার করবেন বলবে যে বাজেট নাই পরে দেখবো তোমার ব্যাপারে, এইটাই কোম্পানির লিমিট, এইটাই আমাকে যা লিমিট দিসিলো সবই তো তোমাকে দিয়ে দিলাম, ইত্যাদি। অন্যদিকে রুম থেকে বের হয়ে শুনবেন অন্য টিমের মানুষ আপনার ৩ গুণ রেইজ পাচ্ছে। খুবই আনফেয়ার। কোন প্রপার রিকগনিশন নাই। এমএল নাহয় এআই টিমের নাম শুনে পটে যায়েন না। শুধু এক চার্ন এনালাইসিস করতেসে ২০ বছর ধরে কিন্তু কোন ধরনের নিজস্বতা নাই, কোন জেনুইন রিসার্চ নাই। ফ্যাসিলিটি ভালো। তবে ম্যানেজার ভালো না পড়লে জীবন ত্যানা বানায়ে ফেলে। বাহির থেকে এক কোম্পানি মনে হইলেও ভেতরে অনেক টিম এবং একেকটা আলাদা আলাদা চলে। সেই সমস্যাতেই জর্জরিত।

title: Once a paradise, now fading into earth’s embrace
content:
It used to be one of the best places in Bangladesh for software engineers. It still is, but all the good things are gradually fading away.
Pros:
One of the best working environment and engineering culture in Bangladesh, if not the best.
The flexibility, work life balance, and other benefits are awesome.
You can work from anywhere, as long as your manager approves.
The engineers here are really talented and amazing people. You get the chance to learn a lot from them.
There are a lot of initiatives that help engineers to learn and improve their skills. They often organize knowledge transfer sessions, tech talks, hack days and other initiatives to keep engineers interested.
Everyone here is very supportive. A great place for everyone, from freshers to senior engineers.
The food is good, and there are bottomless snacks for you if your mouth feels lonely.
Cons:
Many good benefits are being reduced day by day in the name of cost cutting and budget management.
Used to have unlimited PTOs earlier, which was a great thing. But now there's limited number of PTOs.
The office space is small compared to the number of employees. Normally it's fine because many employees work from home most of the days. But on occasions when more people visit the office, some people can't find a place to sit.

title: কফটিমাইজলি
content:
একদা একটি ছোট্ট কফি শপ ছিল। মালিক নিজেই যত্ন সহকারে বিশেষ উপকরণ দিয়ে কফি বানাতেন।
একদিন বড় চেইন কোম্পানি সেটি কিনে নিল। নতুন ম্যানেজার বললেন, "এত কষ্ট করে কেন? মেশিন দিয়েই তো কফি দ্রুত বানানো যায়! কফটিমাইজলি বলে কথা!!"
মালিক বললেন, "স্যার, এটা তো আমার হাতের ছোঁয়া, প্রতিটি কাপে ভালবাসা যায়।"
কিছুদিন পর দেখা গেল যে এখনঃ
প্যাকেটের পাউডার থেকে মেশিন দিয়ে কফি বানানো হচ্ছে
অর্ধেক উপকরণ বাদ দেওয়া হয়েছে
কফির গুণগত মান নিশ্চিত করার জন্য চার স্তরের নিরাপত্তা বলয় তৈরি করা হয়েছে
দোকানের কর্মীদের সুযোগ সুবিধাও কমে গেছে
একদিন মালিক ম্যানেজারকে জিজ্ঞেস করলেন, "আপনি কি জানেন আমাদের কফির স্বাদ কতটা কমে গেছে?"
ম্যানেজার মৃদু হেসে বললেন, "আরে ভাই, লাভ তো বেড়েছে! কাস্টমার তো আছে! আর তাছাড়া আশেপাশে তাকান। কফি তো কফি, ৫ টাকার চায়ের দোকানও নেই কোথাও।"
মালিক মনে মনে ভাবলেন, "হ্যাঁ, কাস্টমার আছে বটে, কফির দোকানও আছে, কিন্তু কফির আত্মা যে আর নেই..."
বিশেষ দ্রষ্টব্যঃ গল্পের প্রতিটি চরিত্র কাল্পনিক। কাল্পনিক গল্পের সাথে বাস্তবতা মিলে গেলে তার দায় লেখক নেবে না।

title: Bhai ektu thakte den

title: আগেই ভালো ছিলাম
content: ধরেন প্রথম বিশ্বের একটি দেশ থেকে দ্বিতীয় বিশ্বের একটি দেশে গেলেন। মনকে সান্ত্বনা দিতে পারবেন যে অন্তত তৃতীয় বিশ্বের কোন দেশে যান নাই।
